meats.title: Why GLP-1 changes hunger signals

beats.text: After a meal, your gut releases a hormone called GLP-1.
It tells the brain's appetite centers you've had enough, and it slows stomach emptying.
Semaglutide is a medicine that acts on the same receptor, so those signals can be amplified.
It's a medicine, not a shortcut, and a provider decides if it's appropriate.

caption_bodies: GLP-1 is a gut hormone that signals fullness to the brain and slows stomach emptying. Semaglutide acts on that same receptor. A provider decides if it's appropriate.

meats.title: What compounded means

beats.text: One word deserves a clear definition. Compounded.
Compounded semaglutide is prepared by a licensed pharmacy for an individual patient.
It is not FDA-approved. It's considered only when legally available and clinically appropriate.
Your provider decides whether it fits, and prescribing is never guaranteed.

meats.title: Side effects, plainly

beats.text: Every medicine has side effects. Here are the plain facts.
Common ones are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation.
Serious risks include pancreatitis and gallbladder problems. Tell your provider about any severe symptoms.
It's compounded and not FDA-approved. A provider decides if it's right for you.

meats.title: Hunger is a signal

beats.text: Willpower is one weight on a balance. Biology adds weight too: hormones, and gut-to-brain signals.
After a meal, your gut broadcasts a fullness signal. Your brain tunes in like a radio, with hunger as part of the static.
GLP-1 is one of those signals. Semaglutide is a medicine built to act on the GLP-1 receptor, like a key made for one lock.
That receptor plays a part in how appetite centers in the brain respond.
It can also slow how fast the stomach empties, like a conveyor belt running slower.
Beema Health offers compounded semaglutide. A licensed pharmacy prepares it for each patient.
To be clear, compounded semaglutide is not FDA-approved.
